chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, is not unjust to His servants. He is more Knowing of what is in the breasts, more Seeing of what is in the eyes, and closer to them than the jugular vein. He records deeds and recompenses for them, and He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.
ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about Allah's justice and knowledge of the heart?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to reinforce the Shia doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*), asserting that Allah’s omnipresence and meticulous recording of both manifest actions and hidden intentions preclude any possibility of arbitrary punishment. This emphasis on the duality of outward and inward awareness serves as a theological foundation for the concept of *Hisab* (accountability), ensuring that no deed, whether public or private, escapes the All-Knowing (*Al-Alim*).
